nx_a6_bc_001: Unconscious mouth care is an aspiration question: side-lying position, small amounts of fluid, suction ready. Any option performed supine or pouring liquids fails the airway test.
nx_a6_bc_002: Stocking SATA: measure for size, apply before rising while legs are least swollen, smooth wrinkles, remove and inspect per shift. Options rolling the tops or applying to dependent swollen legs are the traps.
nx_a6_bc_003: Enema positioning is anatomy: left side (Sims') with the right knee flexed follows the descending colon. Options offering supine or right side ignore where the fluid must travel.
nx_a6_bc_004: 'Alongside the prescribed regimen' invites complementary measures: heat, positioning, relaxation, distraction. Reject options that replace medication or promise cure - adjuncts add, never substitute.
nx_a6_bc_005: Passive ROM technique: support the joint above and below, move slowly to the point of resistance, never past pain. Any option that stretches through pain converts therapy into injury.
nx_a6_bc_006: Incontinence skin protection is barrier plus prompt cleansing - moisture is the enemy. Options relying on indwelling catheters trade a skin problem for an infection risk, which NCLEX penalises.
nx_a6_bc_007: Intake counts anything liquid at room temperature: ice chips count at roughly half their volume, gelatin counts, solid food does not. The option list is testing the ice-chips rule.
nx_a6_bc_008: Hearing-aid care: remove before showering, clean with a dry soft cloth, open the battery door at night, keep away from heat. Water and solvent options are the planted errors.
nx_a6_hp_001: Solids start around 6 months with iron-fortified single-ingredient foods, one new food every few days to spot reactions. Options starting cereal in the bottle or before 4 months contradict guidance.
nx_a6_hp_002: A 15-month-old rides rear-facing in the back seat until reaching the seat's rear-facing limits: the correct statement keeps the child rear-facing; turning forward at the first birthday is the classic error.
nx_a6_hp_003: Preconception teaching is folic acid daily BEFORE conception - neural tube closure happens before most people know they are pregnant, so 'start when the test is positive' options are too late.
nx_a6_hp_004: Skin-cancer SATA: broad-spectrum sunscreen reapplied regularly, shade in peak hours, protective clothing, no tanning beds, and skin self-checks. Any option normalising 'base tans' is wrong.
nx_a6_hp_005: Bone-density protection ranks weight-bearing exercise plus adequate calcium and vitamin D first - the lifestyle trio beats any single supplement answer in a 'most appropriate' frame.
nx_a6_hp_006: STI-prevention statements are graded on risk realism: correct understanding acknowledges barrier methods reduce but do not eliminate risk, and that many infections are asymptomatic - screen options for false absolutes.
nx_a6_hp_007: Concussion return-to-play is a medical-clearance rule: no same-day return, symptom-free progression under professional evaluation. Any option letting the coach or the score decide is wrong.
nx_a6_hp_008: At 12 months: brush twice daily with a smear of fluoride toothpaste, first dental visit by the first birthday, no bottle in bed. The bedtime-bottle option is the caries trap.
nx_a6_ps_001: Acute mania priorities are physiologic: finger foods and fluids the client can consume while moving, rest periods, low stimulation. Insight-oriented options ignore that the body is depleting first.
nx_a6_ps_002: Early OCD care allows the ritual while scheduling around it - abruptly blocking compulsions spikes anxiety. The correct option limits gradually; the 'stop the washing now' option is the trap.
nx_a6_ps_003: Sharp last week, altered since yesterday is delirium, not dementia: acute onset and fluctuation demand a search for the physiologic cause - infection, drugs, hypoxia - not a memory-care referral.
nx_a6_ps_004: A caregiver describing exhaustion needs caregiver-focused intervention: respite resources and support. Options that redirect attention to the client's care plan miss who the client of this question is.
nx_a6_ps_005: Covering the site and looking away two days post-mastectomy is an expected early grief response to altered body image: accept the pace, stay present, offer gradual involvement - forcing viewing is the planted error.
nx_a6_ps_006: Systematic desensitization pairs relaxation training with gradual exposure up a fear hierarchy - the answer describing 'relaxation plus step-by-step exposure' is definitionally correct; flooding options describe a different therapy.
nx_a6_ps_007: Somatic symptom disorder care is consistency: scheduled brief contacts with one provider team, symptoms acknowledged as real, minimal new workups. Options that either dismiss symptoms or escalate testing both feed the cycle.
nx_a6_ps_008: Bedwetting and clinginess in a hospitalized 5-year-old is regression - an expected stress response: respond with acceptance and comfort, never punishment or toilet-retraining pressure during the crisis.
nx_a7_si_001: Client on the floor: assess before moving - injury check first, then help up with adequate assistance, then notify and document. Any option that lifts first or fills out the report first has the sequence backwards.
nx_a7_si_002: Tornado response moves clients away from windows into interior corridors, closes doors and blinds, and continues essential care. Evacuation options belong to fire scenarios - matching disaster to response is the whole question.
nx_a7_si_003: Scabies takes contact precautions - gown and gloves - plus treatment of close contacts and bagging of linens. Airborne or droplet options misclassify a skin-to-skin parasite.
nx_a7_si_004: Needlestick sequence: wash with soap and water immediately, then report and seek evaluation per protocol for post-exposure prophylaxis timing. Options that squeeze the wound or delay reporting fail.
nx_a7_si_005: Hydroxyzine next to hydralazine is a look-alike/sound-alike hazard: the systems answer - separate storage, tall-man lettering, report to the safety process - beats any 'be more careful' option.
nx_a7_si_006: Home safety for low vision: lighting on stairs and pathways, contrast marking on step edges, clutter and loose rugs removed, handrails. Accept environment-changing options; reject behaviour-only advice.
nx_a7_rr_001: Evisceration: cover the bowel with sterile saline-moistened gauze, position supine with knees flexed, NPO, urgent notification - never push anything back in. The moist-dressing option is the non-negotiable.
nx_a7_rr_002: After transvenous pacemaker insertion, limit the affected arm's elevation and monitor rhythm plus the insertion site - the correct option restricts left-arm raising; range-of-motion encouragement is the trap.
nx_a7_rr_003: Post-thoracentesis, report respiratory distress signs - increasing dyspnea, asymmetric breath sounds, tracheal shift - which spell pneumothorax. Mild site soreness options are expected findings planted as decoys.
nx_a7_rr_004: EEG preparation: clean hair, no caffeine, take usual medications unless told otherwise, and possibly reduced sleep if a sleep-deprived study is ordered. The caffeine and hair-product options are the details tested.
nx_a7_rr_005: After polypectomy the report-now symptom is significant bleeding or severe abdominal pain - perforation and hemorrhage signs. Gas and mild cramping options are expected post-insufflation findings.
nx_a7_rr_006: Swollen, cool, pale site with occlusion alarm is infiltration: stop the infusion and remove the line, elevate, and restart elsewhere. Options that slow the rate or flush the line push fluid into tissue.
nx_a7_mc_001: Bedside report with a visitor present is a privacy question: ask the client's permission before proceeding. Options that continue automatically or eject the visitor both skip the client's choice.
nx_a7_mc_002: Delegation to assistive personnel follows the stable-client, routine-task, predictable-outcome rule: vital signs on stable clients, ambulation, hygiene. Anything involving assessment, teaching, or an unstable client stays with the nurse.
nx_a7_mc_003: Conscientious objection is prospective: arrange alternative coverage through proper channels in advance, never abandon the client at hand. The correct option secures coverage; refusal-at-the-bedside options are abandonment.
nx_a7_mc_004: A CAUTI cluster gets a systems response: audit against the bundle, review catheter necessity daily, re-educate. Options that single out individual nurses for blame contradict just-culture principles.
nx_a7_pa_001: The silent chest is the emergency: wheezing that disappears while distress continues means airflow has nearly stopped - escalate immediately. Reading quiet as improvement is the deadliest trap in respiratory items.
nx_a7_pa_002: Profound dehydration, extreme glucose, minimal ketones in an older type 2 client is HHS: the first priority is aggressive fluid resuscitation per orders, with insulin after volume - reversing that order is the distractor.
nx_a7_pa_003: 41 C with hot DRY skin and confusion is heat stroke, not exhaustion: rapid active cooling is the intervention that saves the brain - options offering oral fluids to a confused client also fail the airway test.
nx_a7_pa_004: Addison's plus vomiting plus missed hydrocortisone is impending adrenal crisis: parenteral steroid replacement and fluids now. Any option that reschedules oral dosing misreads the physiology of dependence.
nx_a7_bc_001: CPAP abandonment over mask leaks is an equipment-fit problem: arrange mask refitting and follow-up rather than documenting noncompliance - fix the barrier, keep the therapy.
nx_a7_bc_002: Fragile-skin bathing: warm (not hot) water, pH-balanced or no-rinse cleansers, pat dry, moisturise. Hot water and vigorous rubbing options strip what little barrier remains.
nx_a7_bc_003: Neuropathic foot care: inspect daily with a mirror, test water with the elbow or thermometer, well-fitting shoes always, professional nail care for thick nails - reject barefoot, heating pads, and bathroom surgery.
nx_a7_bc_004: Lumbar puncture positioning maximises interspinous space: side-lying with knees to chest and chin down (or sitting leaning over a table). The fetal-curl option is correct by geometry.
